newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares take breather, undertone positive.
newsitem.headline: German shares take breather, undertone positive.

text.p: German shares paused for breath on Tuesday after a surge of over three percent on Monday, but traders were optimistic that the market would continue to climb once the new levels had been established.
Traders said they now saw the 30-share DAX index in a broad range of 3,320 to 3,390 points. The index stood 18.84 points or 0.57 percent higher at 3,331.72 points at 0910 GMT.
Among positive factors for the market was the strong dollar, which was trading at around 1.7150 marks, helping export stocks to climb.

Dealers said they would continue to watch Wall Street carefully and that the market would remain nervous of further falls for some time, although the stabilisation seen over the last few days provided an injection of confidence.
Better news from the domestic jobs market had little impact however. Unemployment fell to a non-adjusted level of 4.48 million in March from 4.67 million in February.

The federal labour office, reporting a fall in March jobless, predicted a further fall in April and said a government forecast for an average unemployment level of 4.2 million in 1997 could still be achieved.
